item.title: Rats dead and alive all around the area, 26th August
item.description:
Rats nests around this area, also dead rats in the bushes smelling awful. I tried to report it via the Bromley website at the Pest portal ut the portal is experiencing technical issues. The situation has been going on for a while. Pest control should come to investigate and put traps. Around the bushes behind bus Stop P in Anerley Hill, on the left hand and right hand side of the bushes near the trees there are rat nests. Also rats come out the bush on the right hand side of the bus stop where the green antenna is, near the bike rack. The centre of this area infested is what3words location ///bother.wings.hiding

item.title: Forest hire bike obstructing the public footway (and driver sightline) fronting Holy Trinity Church, 64, Lennard Rd, Penge., 26th August
item.description:
Forest hire bike obstructing the public footway (and driver sightline) fronting Holy Trinity Church, 64, Lennard Rd, Penge. Seen at 11.58am Wed 26/8/26. In news media reports, and posts by Liam Conlon MP, neither Lime nor Forest hire bike companies have agreements with the L B of Bromley to operate in the borough. Both companies have agreed to cease trading in Bromley until such time as an agreement is made, ceasing as of Monday 25/8/26 (MSN news extract quoting the Bromley Transport and Highways Portfolio Holder). Please remove the footway obstruction ASAP to a secure contractor compound, inform Forest and prosecute / fine the company as appropriate for the offence, as an example and to abate the hazard for persons with visual disability etc. I am informed of the following: "Councils can utilise powers under Section 149 of the Highways Act 1980, which allows highway authorities to immediately remove items causing a danger or obstruction on public footways and roads."

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 66, Lennard Road, Penge, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
